claims.text: The as-cast or conventionally cooled eutectic high-entropy alloy has coarse eutectic lamellae.
Hot forging followed immediately by rapid quenching refines eutectic lamellar spacing.
The proposed processing transforms coarse eutectic colonies into a uniformly refined, partially equiaxed microstructure.
The proposed processing produces well-distributed eutectic phases.
Processing near 0.7 T_m with sufficient dwell time allows dynamic recrystallization.
Rapid quenching after forging prevents microstructural coarsening.
Rapid quenching locks in the refined microstructure.
Refined lamellar spacing increases interfacial or grain-boundary area.
The increased boundary area impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Improved phase dispersion enables more homogeneous deformation and effective load partitioning.
More homogeneous deformation delays crack initiation and propagation.
Delayed crack initiation and propagation enhance ductility.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the processing will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30%.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the processing will maintain or modestly improve uniform tensile elongation.
Refining the lamellar spacing beyond an optimum can cause embrittlement.
Poorly controlled processing can compromise the strength–ductility balance.
The quantitative improvement depends on alloy composition, processing parameters, and component scale.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says ductility will increase, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule permit ductility merely to be maintained. Thus, an outcome with no ductility increase could pass the stated test despite not satisfying the headline hypothesis.
